trickyParts: write_corpus_test.go must compile unchanged at main, so the base and head dumps can be compared with cmp; it uses no head-only symbol.
liveOperation.abandon releases the fork on a panic whatever updates holds, because ygo emits no update when its phase 2 is aborted (buildPhase2, or a type observer before OnUpdate).
deviations: The replay CPU gate (A1) was not run as paired runs. sjawhar/legion#2448 removed MarkQuote's third read on main before the head runs, so the expected gain is near 0 at the current base. The architect decided that the CPU part is written up on INFRA-512 (dispatch://INFRA-512/comment/ad919553-ec42-46b6-9321-87dd191e3b5a), and that only parts with their own evidence merge.
C1 (reading the anchor inside the write) was dropped by the architect's criterion 2: the API cannot reach the refusal, and a rolled-back refusal leaves the same state on main and head.
pmdoc.ReadUnshared (INFRA-692) is not adopted: INFRA-692 has not merged. The architect gives it to a later child.

The forced-GC heap check (A4) was not run, because no replay head runs were made. The change keeps no new state: the reuse returns the tree the write already holds, and the counters are two atomic integers.
Round 1: the real-size proof of the rendering reuse stays in the HTTP equivalence run and the benchmark; go test runs on a 7.3 KB document so envoy-go-race fits its limit.
